summary: A rival's objection to a candidate's nomination papers is upheld because the papers came in before the window opened.
realLife: An electoral board removed a mayoral candidate after an objector argued her nomination papers were filed before the legal window; her side said election officials had told them the timing was fine, and they planned to appeal.
sources: Shaw Local, candidate bounced from the ballot for mayor, Nov. 20, 2024: https://www.shawlocal.com/daily-chronicle/2024/11/20/linh-nguyen-bounced-from-2025-ballot-for-dekalb-mayor/
inGame: needs: an objection step with a hearing by a local board, and a filing window the clerk enforces

turns.pulledBy: a window that was clear and met
turns.writesBack: the candidate stays and the objector's fee is lost

turns.turn: The board upholds it and the candidate turns to write-in
turns.writesBack: a name off the ballot and a write-in plan
